newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank warns pace of inflation has picked up.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank warns pace of inflation has picked up.

text.p: The Bundesbank warned on Wednesday that the pace of consumer price increases had picked up in the last few months and that it would be steering its policy to ensure inflation remained under control.
In its August monthly report, the central bank said: "It cannot be overlooked that there has been a stronger rise in consumer prices in the last few months."
"The Bundesbank will orientate its policy in such a way that price stability, which has been essentially achieved, can be maintained," it added.

The Bundesbank's statements would appear to support the view prevalent in financial markets that the Bundesbank is moving very close to tightening its monetary policy, a move which would end five years of falling interest rates.

Recent sharp slides in the mark have been seen as the main reason prompting a potential central bank move, but the Bundesbank itself -- in the form of its chief economist, Otmar Issing -- has also started to utter other economic concerns which would point to a rate rise.

In interviews published last week, Issing pointed to high capacity utilisation and price pressures at various levels of the economy -- alongside general concern that the mark has weakened against the mark steadily this year.
The central bank refrained from adjusting its main money market rate, the repo, on Tuesday but markets believe a move is in the pipeline nonetheless.
In its report, the Bundesbank repeated recent comments that it was watching the currency markets closely, linking this firmly to the potential influence of mark losses on prices.
"The Bundesbank will observe further currency rate developments closely with a view to the risks presented for price stability," it said.

A weaker currency holds the risk of imported inflation as import prices are boosted. The central bank noted in its report that this impact of the mark's drop had been limited so far only because dollar-denominated raw material prices had fallen.
The dollar has gained over 20 percent against the mark this year to stand about 38 percent above its all-time low of 1.3450 marks.
